solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cut what bridegroom did

blocks.note: first meaning: chopped, as with an axe
second meaning, split in two: the groom is a man who got married

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful split: HE WED is exactly what a bridegroom did, and run together it makes the past tense of hew.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to chop with an axe, so something hewed has been chopped or shaped by blows.

clue.text: Breathe in groggily and go to sleep

indicators.note: groggy movement is unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drowsy person inhales unsteadily and nods off.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that hibernate pass the winter in a deep dormant state, a long sleep.

clue.text: War cry from that corps regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

blocks.note: that and who are interchangeable relative pronouns, as in the man that came
the second and fourth letters of corps

explanation.surface: A battle shout rises from a military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War cry from that corps' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'cry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud excited shout, the kind raised as a battle yell.

clue.text: A couple of hours pet-sitting?

blocks.note: surface reading: a short spell spent minding someone's animal
setter's reading: a two-hour shift on board ship, whose name contains a pet and the act of keeping watch

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that keeping an eye on a pet is a playful reading of a naval term.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the dogwatches are the two short two-hour watches from 4pm to 8pm.

clue.text: Very obvious trail grew confused

indicators.note: letters that are confused are mixed up and fall into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A path through the undergrowth has become tangled and overgrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Something writ large is stated in big letters, plainly on display, so the idiom means conspicuous.

clue.text: Engineer's question heard by some

indicators.note: heard means it is the sound that counts, and only in some accents do the two match

blocks.note: the questioning word, said without the aspirated wh

explanation.surface: An engineer's query is overheard by a few people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer's' looks possessive, but the 's is is: the engineer is the sound of a question.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine; the unit of power bears his name.

clue.text: I can be shown to be less than perfect

blocks.note: first meaning: my truth can be demonstrated
second meaning: capable of being made better

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I'M PROVABLE and it says the first part of the clue; read whole, it means capable of improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that can still be improved has room to get better, so it falls short of flawless.

clue.text: Historian covering royal uniform

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it so it sits inside

blocks.note: Livy was a Roman historian
ER, Elizabeth Regina, marks something royal

explanation.surface: A historian writes about what the royal household wears.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants or staff of a household or company.

clue.text: For City, the scorer is unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters take an odd new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football fan notes that City's goalscorer is a rare talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' suggests a football club such as Manchester City; it is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester is a cathedral city in Kent, England, and also a city in New York State.

clue.text: Like an aristocrat perhaps to be in plenty of time?

blocks.note: first meaning, read as earl-y: like an earl
second meaning: ahead of schedule

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a jokey coinage: adding -y to earl, the noble title, makes an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving early means arriving before the appointed hour, with time to spare.

clue.text: Mentioned having purchased everything available around river

indicators.note: one thing placed around another wraps it, holding it inside

blocks.note: to buy up is to purchase the whole stock
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone discussed how they had cleared the shelves of everything for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: R sits inside BOUGHT UP, after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a subject is to raise it in conversation, so a topic brought up has been mentioned.

clue.text: Serviceman: see one at attention endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut away

blocks.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see
the Roman numeral for one
care is attention paid to something

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to watch someone standing to attention on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceman' suggests the army; here it is a man who leads church services.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest who conducts church services, hence a cheeky serviceman.

clue.text: Ring again to cancel

blocks.note: first meaning: peal bells once more
second meaning: revoke a law

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the word as RE (again) and PEAL (ring), the sense a bell-ringer would use.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament repeals an act when it revokes it, so the law is annulled.

clue.text: Put sport back in modest setting, showing consideration

indicators.note: going back means these words run from right to left
placed in a setting means held inside its frame, like a gem in a ring mount

blocks.note: to set something is to put it down
RU is rugby union
coy means shy or modest

explanation.surface: Instructions to return a sports item to its humble place, done politely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' looks like an instruction, but it supplies letters of its own; RU for rugby union is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy is polite regard for others, the same as showing thoughtful consideration.

clue.text: One's little room covered in a lot of jumble

indicators.note: something covered in another thing is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: many means a lot
I for one plus the 's
a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: Someone's tiny room is buried under a heap of clutter.
explanation.walkthrough: One's gives IS because the Roman numeral I stands for one and the 's is the verb is.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a mixed collection of assorted items, a varied jumble.

clue.text: Disappointment ain't turned about by acquiring capital

indicators.note: letters that are turned over are rearranged into another order
acquiring something means taking it in, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
C is circa, about
Lima is the capital of Peru
X is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A letdown when a slangy word gets turned around by a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' does double duty in the surface as a preposition; here it is the times sign, as in three by four, and joins 'about' around the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax is a disappointing end after a build-up of expectation, a letdown.

clue.text: Gets side-tracked, needing time for introduction for Cats

indicators.note: swapping in for the introduction means the opening letter is replaced

blocks.note: to digress is to wander off the subject
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A rambling speaker needs a time slot to introduce the musical Cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' looks like the Lloyd Webber show; it is the definition for big female felines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigresses are female tigers, which are big cats.

clue.text: Obstinate, not born to be a butt

indicators.note: not having something means that portion is taken out

blocks.note: stubborn means obstinate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is stubborn by nature rather than born a figure of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short end left over, like a cigarette butt or the remaining part of a ticket.

clue.text: Luxuriant condition of hair is prominent in coach

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

blocks.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
to shine is to stand out or excel

explanation.surface: Someone's thick, glossy hair stands out on the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushiness is the quality of being thick and dense, as with a full head of hair.

clue.text: Riddle of shoes son moved to the furthest possible place

indicators.text: son moved to the furthest possible place
indicators.note: the letter for son travels from one extreme of the word to the other end

blocks.note: trainers are sports shoes; the S of son is the last letter

explanation.surface: A puzzle about shoes and a boy who has wandered as far away as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' suggests a puzzle, but a riddle is also a coarse sieve; S moves from the end of TRAINERS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a large coarse sieve for soil or gravel, so a strainer is the same tool.

clue.text: Irritable in overheated gym

indicators.note: in tells the solver to look inside the following words for a run of letters

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A stuffy, overheated gym makes people tetchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and nervous, quick to snap, so it is a near synonym of irritable.

clue.text: Figures sulphur preparations in lab must be contaminated by phosphorus

indicators.note: something contaminated has foreign matter introduced into it

blocks.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
cultures are grown samples prepared in a laboratory
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A chemistry-lab warning that sulphur samples are being spoiled by phosphorus.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes into CULTURES after the L, with S in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculptures are carved or modelled statues, and a figure is such a representation of a body.

clue.text: Let oneself down in trouble concealing disease

indicators.note: concealing means holding something hidden inside

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: Someone disappoints themselves by hiding an illness that troubles them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let oneself down' reads as disappointing yourself; it is literal descent on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a rock face by a rope, literally lowering oneself.

clue.text: Small garden area, plain with patches of colour

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Kew is a district of London famous for its botanical gardens
bald means plain or unadorned, as in a bald statement

explanation.surface: A little patch of garden is plain but for some colourful spots.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewbald describes a horse with irregular patches of white and another colour, usually not black.

clue.text: News at last due for broadcast

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter

blocks.note: the final letter of News
a sum due is owed

explanation.surface: The news is finally ready to go on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio or TV; here it means scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter it widely by hand, so sowed is its past tense synonym.

clue.text: I appreciate that popular number one: it's in South Pacific

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thank you
a hit is a popular song
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Thanking someone for a favourite song from the musical South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: South Pacific is also a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical full of popular numbers, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia, located in the southern Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Poem of the millennium overlooked by church

indicators.note: in a down light, something overlooked sits beneath what looks down on it, so removing the top leaves it

blocks.note: a chiliad is a thousand years
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A poem from the millennium is ignored by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the poem with CH placed above it in the grid makes CHILIAD, a millennium.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic poem about the siege of Troy.

clue.text: Bill for example's taken first oath

blocks.note: e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for example
an ad, like a bill, is a poster or advertisement

explanation.surface: A man named Bill, say, has sworn an oath first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a notice. 'Taken first' puts the example before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old mild exclamation, a minced form of by God, so it counts as an oath.

clue.text: Rubbish in middle of ship picked up

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio means heard rather than read

blocks.note: the waist is the middle part of a ship's deck

explanation.surface: Garbage is found lying amidships.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is unwanted material thrown away, the same thing as rubbish.

clue.text: Bright and shiny chap in elite force not taking sides

indicators.note: without sides means both outer letters are dropped
in means placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: a gent is a man
the Marines are a crack fighting force

explanation.surface: A dazzling man serving in a crack unit stays neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: MARINES loses M and S to leave ARINE, which then holds GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentine means silvery, from the Latin for silver, so it describes a bright shiny metal look.

clue.text: One spread out on back of board, as shown

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the final letter of board
the Roman numeral for one
splayed means spread out wide

explanation.surface: Someone sprawled across the back of a board for everyone to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Displayed means put on view, exhibited, which is what something shown has been.

clue.text: Travels with no man born in British Isles

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so those parts are taken out

blocks.note: the Hebrides are islands off western Scotland
he is a male person
B is the abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: Someone tours the British Isles without a man born there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British Isles' looks like the whole archipelago, but it means one group of islands within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to journey on a horse, bike or vehicle, so rides is a synonym of travels.
